profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 45 (CyrusOne missing-address campaign): matched this rows own three building NVA1 through NVA3 campus name to three independent aggregator sources all agreeing on the same shared campus address.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne is a large scale data center provider headquartered in Dallas, Texas. In 2016 CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchanges original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly 130 million dollars, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15 year lease. In November 2021, KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately 15 billion dollar deal, taking the company private, and that acquisition closed in 2022. CyrusOne has operated as a privately held company since, a company level ownership fact this registry had not previously recorded with a citable source. This specific row, NVA1, NVA2 and NVA3, corresponds to this operators own three building Sterling, Virginia campus, distinct from the separate NVA9 and Sterling IX facility addressed elsewhere in this registry. Three independent sources, a colocation marketplace listing from Inflect, a datacenterHawk listing for NVA1, and a datacentermap listing for NVA2, all fetched fresh this session, agree on 21111 Ridgetop Circle, Sterling, Virginia as the shared campus address for these three buildings. The operators own current page for this campus, also fetched fresh this session, confirms the Sterling, VA, Loudoun County location but does not itself publish a street address.
sources_tried: The operators own current campus page confirming the Sterling, VA location without a street address, resolved via three independent aggregator sources all agreeing on the same shared campus address for this three building NVA1 through NVA3 campus

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling, Virginia campus spans three connected buildings with 44 megawatts of published IT capacity, making it a mid-scale colocation facility in a major East Coast data center cluster.

The facility's capacity sits well below hyperscale standards but reflects the economics of the colocation model, where CyrusOne leases space to multiple tenants rather than operating as a single-tenant enterprise infrastructure. Sterling itself sits in Loudoun County, part of Northern Virginia's concentration of data centers that benefit from proximity to Washington, D.C., established telecommunications routes, and regional power availability. The 420,000 square feet across three buildings suggests substantial operational complexity, though the campus address was confirmed only through third-party aggregator sources rather than the operator's own published materials.

The data does not specify when these buildings entered service, their current utilization rate, power supply sources, or whether they serve AI workloads specifically versus general colocation demand. It also does not indicate whether the 44 megawatt figure represents nameplate capacity, available capacity, or actual draw. CyrusOne's 2022 transition to private ownership under KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners may influence future expansion or specialization, but that shift's relevance to this facility's trajectory remains unclear from the available record.
